title: "Stage 4 – The menu and the declaration"
case: housing
---
::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at the menu](../../slides/housing-one-day-methods.html#/the-specification-menu){target="_blank"}, in Part 3, in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

The second stage of the housing-audit case works the menu of defensible analyses, one decision at a time, and ends on the one analysis that you would defend, declared in the preregistration block of your report before it runs. The rest of the stage reads the curve of the claim and the replication with new data at a slower pace, and finishes the first case report, in about six hours of work all told.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| [Specification menu](../../cases/housing/menu.qmd) | The estimand statement, the eleven decisions at three levels, the five on which the curve keeps more than one option and the 64 specifications that they make, the worked example, and the rules for declaring and reporting a result. | 30 minutes |
| Slides, the menu and the methods in Part 3 | The ground rules of the menu: change one decision at a time, and read the reason when an option is refused. Then a difference in proportions and the linear probability model set against the logit, and the optional run on odds ratios, standard errors for a 0/1 outcome, the choice of test, the randomisation test, covariates in an experiment and the subgroups beside the curve, which the `d` key shows and hides. | 30 minutes |
| Task 4 in your report or working script, or [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-4-menu) Task 4 | Call `try_spec()` with no arguments for the reference specification, then three or four times more, changing one argument at a time, and compare the tries with `my_experiments()`. Ask once for an option off the curve, such as `model = "three_group"`, to read why it is refused. If you want your exploration on the [class chart](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd#class-results), send the try that you would defend with `submit_exploration()`; it appears there as an open circle. | 30 minutes |
| Slides, [Part 4](../../slides/housing-one-day-methods.html#/part-4-multiverse-replication-and-preregistration){target="_blank"} | Your own small multiverse; the curve of 64 with the published result and the five analysts on it; the class chart, which holds the results of earlier cohorts; what moved the estimate; the SCORE replication with new names and the power of the two designs; the critics of the multiverse; and what a preregistration settles and what it leaves open. | 45 minutes |
| The preregistration block in your report, or [browser lab](../../cases/housing/lab.qmd#task-5-preregistration) Task 5 | Complete the block before you run anything: the claim, the data-in-hand statement, one option for each decision, a sentence from your causal graph on why the specification answers the claim, and your rule for what supports or undermines it. Render the report and keep the rendered copy, which carries the date on which it was rendered. Then fit the specification with `run_spec()`, and send it with `report_result()` if you want it on the chart, where it appears as a filled circle. | 30 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/housing/multiverse.qmd) | Reading the curve, the reference marks, what moved the estimate, and the displays beside the curve: the other outcomes and the Black names, the subgroups, and the randomisation distribution. | 40 minutes |
| [Audit experiments](../../companion/experiments.qmd), from [Randomisation inference](../../companion/experiments.qmd#sec-ri) to [The ethics of deception](../../companion/experiments.qmd#sec-ethics), and [the replication](../../cases/housing/index.qmd#sec-replication) in the case study | Randomisation inference; power, and why significant estimates from small studies tend to be too large; the ethics of deceiving officials and of publishing data on people who never consented to be studied. Then the design and the result of the preregistered audit of 3,050 housing authorities that SCORE ran, and how to read it beside the curve. | 60 minutes |
| [Causal graphs and adjustment sets](../../companion/dags.qmd#sec-adjustment), the adjustment sets of the curve | The covariates that the curve offers, read off the graph of the case: why none of them confounds the comparison of the names, and what they do among the replies. | 10 minutes |
| [The multiverse and its critics](../../companion/multiverse.qmd), from [Origins](../../companion/multiverse.qmd#sec-origins) to [The multiverse in the classroom](../../companion/multiverse.qmd#sec-teaching) | Where multiverse analysis came from, the three purposes that a multiverse can serve, the debate of 2025–26 read against this small curve on which every specification agrees while the replication failed, robustness against replicability, and the multiverse in teaching. | 60 minutes |
| Your report | Render the report of the workspace with all five tasks complete, the preregistration block as it stood before the run and the result beneath it. This is the first case report. The section "Going further" at its end holds optional exercises that run in the workspace. | 30 minutes |

**Sending results.** Both submissions are optional. A result sent alone joins the class chart of the case beside the results that earlier cohorts sent, and the helpers work exactly as they do in a workshop, filling in the results form for you. Each workspace draws a tag of its own for the chart, so to find your marks in all four cases, give the same nickname every time, as in `submit_exploration(nickname = "blue-heron")`.

**Shortcuts.** If time is short, read only the section on [robustness and replicability](../../companion/multiverse.qmd#sec-replicability) of the multiverse module now, and the rest of it in stage 11, where its section on the EU-frames case builds on it.

**By the end of the stage** you have explored the menu one decision at a time, placed your declared result among the 64 specifications of the curve, completed a preregistration before its specification ran, and rendered the first case report.
